newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong Governor blasts naysayers.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong Governor blasts naysayers.

text.p: Hong Kong's departing colonial Governor Chris Patten on Sunday criticised those who doubted the territory's future and expressed confidence in its people's resilience.
"Even five years ago when I came, people were dipping their pens in a pot of gloom to write about Hong Knng," Patten said in an interview with Hong Kong radio.
"They predicted economic collapse, social polarisation, political turmoil. Well, they were wrong," he said.

Britain will hand over Hong Kong to China at midnight (1600 GMT) on Monday after a colonial interlude of 156 years, and Patten will depart Hong Kong aboard the royal yacht Britannia with Britain's Prince Charles.
The "barren rock" settled by Britain in 1841 has developed into one of the world's most stable and prosperous financial and manufacturing centres.
Hong Kong's stock market closed at an all-time high on Friday before a five-day public holiday dominated by handover festivities.
Patten said he would leave Hong Kong with a sense of pride in his own and Britain's role in the territory's success but spoke warmly of the many quiet times he enjoyed."

"I'll miss my urban expeditions, pottering around Hong Kong, poking through piles of second-hand watches on a kerb-side stall looking for a bargain... enjoying the smells and the sights and energy of this great Chinese maritime city," he said.

"It's sometimes thought rather politically incorrect for public officials to admit to having a good time. But I have to say that I've enjoyed being Governor. Hong Kong, at its best is great fun -- boisterous, noisy, lively and exciting."
